description.narrative: The Project is expected to increase access to finance for MSMEs and sustainable finance-oriented enterprises in renewable energy and Electric Vehicles (EVs), alongside strengthening the resilience of Bangladesh's financial sector. MSMEs face a substantial formal finance gap widened by successive crises. This Project will help City Bank expand lending to trade-oriented MSMEs, supporting enterprise growth and job creation. Furthermore, expanded lending to renewable energy and EV sectors will contribute to emissions reductions and help mobilize the large-scale investment Bangladesh requires under its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC 3.0). The introduction of the DPR structure through this Project will enable Bangladeshi banks to access international capital markets, reducing vulnerability to capital flow disruptions and sustaining productive lending across economic cycles.

The proposed project aims to provide financing of up to US$90 million, for up to 5 years, to City Bank PLC (City Bank or the Bank), a long-standing IFC client, through the first of its kind Diversified Payments Rights (DPR) program established by a bank in Bangladesh. Of the total financing, US$60 million will be for IFCs own account, while the remaining US$30 million will be mobilized (the Project). The proceeds of the investment will be utilized by the Bank to support export- and import-oriented Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) (50%) and sustainable finance assets (50%), including renewable energy, green buildings, and electric vehicles, in Bangladesh.
